examples.ko: 화재 경보기가 갑자기 울려서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The fire alarm suddenly went off and startled me.

examples.ko: 집 천장에 연기 경보기를 새로 달았어요.
examples.en: I installed a new smoke alarm on the ceiling at home.
I replaced the alarm's battery with a new one.
The alarm went off by mistake and firefighters came.

examples.ko: 도난 경보기 소리를 듣고 이웃이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A neighbor came out after hearing the burglar alarm.

examples.ko: 비상구 옆에 경보기가 있는 것 알고 계세요?
examples.en: Did you know there is an alarm next to the emergency exit?

explain: 경보기 앞에 '화재, 도난, 연기'를 붙여서 종류를 말해요. 울리는 소리 자체는 '경보음'이나 '사이렌'이라고 해요. 건물 전체에 울리는 큰 장치는 보통 '비상벨'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: We installed a burglar alarm in the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 훔쳐 가는 일을 알려 주는 장치예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A device that warns of theft.

phrases.en: The alarm suddenly went off at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 날 때는 '울리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 울리다 when it makes a sound.

phrases.en: I quickly turned off the alarm that went off by mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 멈추게 할 때 '끄다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 끄다 when you stop the sound.

explain_en: You put 화재, 도난 or 연기 in front of 경보기 to say what kind it is. The sound itself is called 경보음 or 사이렌. A large device that rings through a whole building is usually called a 비상벨.

en: to be weary; to be tired; to be exhausted

examples.ko: 며칠 야근을 했더니 몸이 너무 곤해요.
examples.en: I worked late for several days, so my body is really worn out.

examples.ko: 아이가 곤하게 자고 있으니까 깨우지 마세요.
examples.en: The child is sleeping soundly, so please don't wake him.

examples.ko: 오늘은 하루 종일 걸어서 다리가 곤했어요.
examples.en: I walked all day today, so my legs were exhausted.

examples.ko: 곤한 몸으로 집에 와서 바로 누웠어요.
examples.en: I came home worn out and lay down right away.

examples.ko: 친구는 소파에서 곤한 잠에 빠져 있었어요.
examples.en: My friend was fast asleep on the sofa.
Mom seemed tired and went to bed early.

explain: '피곤하다'보다 글 느낌이 나고, 몸이 지쳐서 노곤한 느낌이에요. 특히 '곤히 자다', '곤한 잠'처럼 깊이 잠든 모습에 자주 써요. 말할 때 그냥 지쳤다고 하려면 보통 '피곤하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The baby is sleeping soundly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊이 잠든 모습에 가장 자주 쓰는 부사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form most often used for deep sleep.

phrases.en: I haven't woken up from my deep sleep yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 모양으로 명사 '잠'을 꾸미는 정해진 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase where the modifier form describes 잠 (sleep).

phrases.en: You look very weary today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지쳐 보이는 사람의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say someone looks worn out.

explain_en: It feels more literary than '피곤하다' and describes a body worn out and drowsy. It often appears in '곤히 자다' and '곤한 잠' for deep sleep. In plain speech, people usually say '피곤하다' for being tired.

examples.en: The stairs continue in a spiral shape.
The spiral on this shell is pretty.
The smoke rose, drawing a spiral.

examples.ko: 나선처럼 도는 길을 따라 산에 올랐어요.
examples.en: I climbed the mountain along a path that winds like a spiral.
It's a spiral staircase, so it's hard to climb.

examples.ko: 나선은 자연에서 자주 볼 수 있는 모양이에요.
examples.en: Spirals are a shape you often see in nature.

explain: '나선형 계단', '나선 은하'처럼 나선은 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 많이 써요. 원은 처음과 끝이 만나지만 나선은 끝이 열려 있어요. 일상에서는 '빙글빙글', '소용돌이'라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I slowly climb the spiral staircase.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나선'이 모양을 말할 때 가장 흔하게 붙는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way 나선 attaches to describe a shape.

phrases.en: There are many spiral galaxies in space.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학이나 우주 이야기에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase used in science and space topics.

phrases.en: The smoke rises in a spiral.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빙글빙글 도는 모습을 글로 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in writing to describe a swirling movement.

explain_en: 나선 is often attached before another word, as in '나선형 계단' (spiral staircase) or '나선 은하' (spiral galaxy). A circle closes on itself, but a spiral stays open at the end. In daily talk people also say '빙글빙글' (round and round) or '소용돌이' (whirl).

examples.en: The dove symbolizes peace.
The color red symbolized luck in this country.
This building is a place that represents the city.
They say a ring symbolizes a promise.
This painting symbolizes family.

examples.ko: 마음을 상징할 수 있는 모양을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose a shape that can symbolize a feeling.

explain: 비둘기=평화처럼 눈에 보이는 것이 보이지 않는 뜻을 대신할 때 써요. '~은/는 ~을 상징해요' 형태로 말해요. 명사 '상징'은 '평화의 상징'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: A heart is a symbol of love.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사 '상징'을 써서 말하는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 상징 instead of the verb.

phrases.en: This flower is a flower that symbolizes spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifying form that describes the noun after it.

phrases.en: They say white symbolizes cleanliness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 들은 내용이나 일반적인 생각을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to pass on what you have heard or a common belief.

explain_en: Use it when something visible stands for an unseen idea, like a dove for peace. The pattern is '~은/는 ~을 상징해요'. The noun is used as '평화의 상징'.

examples.ko: 높은 하늘에 새털구름이 길게 퍼져 있어요.
examples.en: Wispy cirrus clouds stretch long across the high sky.
Cirrus clouds look really pretty in photos.

examples.ko: 새털구름을 보니 가을이 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: Seeing the wispy clouds, it feels like autumn has come.
The sun is setting between the wispy clouds.
I want to float away lightly like a feather cloud.
The sunset light shines on the cirrus clouds, so the sky is red.

explain: 새의 털처럼 가늘고 길게 퍼진 구름이에요. 과학 시간에는 '권운'이라고도 하지만, 평소 말할 때는 '새털구름'이 더 쉬워요. 뭉게뭉게 솜 같은 '뭉게구름'과는 모양이 달라요.

phrases.en: Cirrus clouds have formed in the autumn sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름이 하늘에 생겼을 때 '끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '끼다' when clouds form in the sky.

phrases.example: 하늘 높이 뜬 새털구름이 정말 예뻐요.
phrases.en: The cirrus clouds high in the sky are really pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 하늘에 있는 구름의 모습을 그릴 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when describing clouds high in the sky.
phrases.en_equiv: cirrus clouds high in the sky

phrases.en: You see lots of cumulus clouds in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새털구름과 달리 솜처럼 뭉쳐 있는 구름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike cirrus clouds, these are puffy, cotton-like clouds.

explain_en: It is a thin, long cloud spread out like bird feathers. In science class it is also called '권운', but in everyday speech '새털구름' is easier. It looks different from the puffy, cotton-like '뭉게구름'.

examples.en: The queen bee lays eggs.
The worker bees gather food for the queen bee.

examples.ko: 벌집 한가운데에서 여왕벌과 일벌들이 함께 살아요.
examples.en: In the middle of the hive, the queen bee and worker bees live together.
They say the hive falls into disorder when the queen bee disappears.

examples.ko: 저는 여왕벌보다 일벌이 더 대단하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think worker bees are more impressive than the queen bee.
In science class, we learned about the life of the queen bee.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '일벌'과 '수벌'이에요. 한 벌집에는 보통 여왕벌이 한 마리 있어요. 과학 시간이나 자연 이야기에서 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: The queen bee and worker bees do different jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 말을 함께 써서 벌집 안의 역할을 비교할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two words are often used together to compare roles in a hive.

phrases.en: One queen bee lives in a beehive.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한 마리'와 함께 수를 셀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 한 마리 when counting.

phrases.en: The worker bees move following the queen bee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌들이 여왕벌 주위에서 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes bees moving around the queen.

explain_en: Its related words are '일벌' (worker bee) and '수벌' (drone). A hive normally has one queen bee. It appears mainly in science class and nature talk.

en: to be elaborate; to be delicate; to be exquisite

examples.ko: 소인국처럼 오밀조밀한 도시가 강 건너에 보였어요.
examples.en: A neat, tightly packed city like a tiny kingdom could be seen across the river.
This room is small but nicely compact, so it's cozy.
I like walking through the snug little alleys.
The inside of the shop is decorated in a neat, compact way.
That painter draws with delicate, close detail.

examples.ko: 집이 오밀조밀하지만 필요한 건 다 있어요.
examples.en: The house is compact, but it has everything you need.

explain: 공간이나 물건, 그림이 작고 촘촘하지만 짜임새 있을 때 써요. 단순히 '좁다'가 아니라 아기자기하게 잘 모여 있다는 좋은 느낌이 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: I like the small but neatly put-together room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 공간이나 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a space or object.

phrases.example: 이 동네는 작은 가게가 많아서 오밀조밀해요.
phrases.en: This neighborhood has lots of little shops packed closely together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 짧게 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite style for briefly stating an impression.

phrases.en: I decorated the small garden in a neat, compact way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 꾸미는 방법을 말하는 부사처럼 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게', it works like an adverb describing how something is done.

explain_en: It is used for spaces, objects or drawings that are small and dense yet well put together. It is not just 'narrow'; it carries a positive sense of being neatly arranged.

examples.en: I drew the notes on the sheet music one by one.
There are so many notes that it is hard to play.

examples.ko: 음표 모양에 따라 소리 길이가 달라요.
examples.en: The length of the sound differs depending on the note shape.
I am learning how to read notes.

examples.ko: 아이 방 벽에 음표 모양 스티커를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put note-shaped stickers on the child's room wall.

examples.ko: 이 악보는 음표를 읽기가 쉬워서 초보자에게 좋아요.
examples.en: The notes in this score are easy to read, so it is good for beginners.

explain: '음표를 읽다', '음표를 그리다'처럼 써요. 쉬는 부분을 나타내는 기호는 '쉼표'라서 '음표'와 짝으로 외워 두면 좋아요. 모양에 따라 '온음표', '2분음표', '4분음표'처럼 불러요.

phrases.en: A quarter note is one beat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음표 모양에 따라 부르는 이름이에요. 숫자가 앞에 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name based on note shape; the number comes first.

phrases.en: Sheet music has notes and rests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 내는 기호와 쉬는 기호를 짝으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the sound symbol with the rest symbol.

phrases.example: 저는 아직 음표를 빨리 못 읽어요.
phrases.en: I still can't read notes quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악보를 보고 음을 알아보는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means recognizing the notes when looking at sheet music.

explain_en: Say '음표를 읽다' or '음표를 그리다'. The symbol for a rest is '쉼표', so it helps to learn the two as a pair. By shape they are named '온음표', '2분음표', and '4분음표'.

en: to be carefree; to be easygoing; to be peaceful (of times)

examples.en: He is always calm and carefree even before something big.

examples.ko: 시험이 내일인데 너무 태평하게 놀고 있어요.
examples.en: The exam is tomorrow, and you're playing around so carelessly.

examples.ko: 태평한 성격 덕분에 스트레스를 별로 안 받아요.
examples.en: Thanks to my easygoing personality, I don't get stressed much.
If you stay this relaxed, you'll miss the train.
With my mind at ease, I fall asleep well too.

examples.ko: 태평해 보이던 친구가 갑자기 울어서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My friend, who looked carefree, suddenly cried and I was surprised.

explain: 걱정 없이 느긋한 모습을 말해요. 성격을 칭찬할 때도 쓰지만, 급한 상황에서 쓰면 '왜 이렇게 여유로워?' 하는 답답함이 담겨요. 반대는 '조급하다'이고, 비슷한 말은 '느긋하다'예요.

phrases.example: 동생은 태평한 성격이라 걱정이 별로 없어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling has an easygoing personality and hardly worries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for describing someone's personality.

phrases.en: He spent the whole vacation carefree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정 없이 느긋하게 시간을 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for spending time relaxed and without worries.

phrases.en: On weekends I eat breakfast at a relaxed pace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이고, '태평하다'보다 답답하다는 느낌이 덜해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word with less of a frustrated tone than '태평하다'.

explain_en: It describes a relaxed, worry-free manner. It can praise someone's personality, but in an urgent situation it carries a feeling of 'why are you so relaxed?'. The opposite is '조급하다', and a similar word is '느긋하다'.

p.n: 태평스럽다 stresses the carefree look or manner.

en: to be blunt; to be curt

examples.ko: 직원의 대답이 너무 퉁명스러워서 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: The staff member's answer was so curt that I felt bad.
That friend's way of speaking is a bit blunt.

examples.ko: 아버지는 퉁명스럽게 대답하셨지만 속은 따뜻한 분이에요.
examples.en: Father answered bluntly, but he's warm inside.
Why are you so curt today of all days?
He answered the phone in a curt voice.
I'm sorry for being so blunt.

explain: 말이나 행동이 친절하지 않고 무뚝뚝해서 듣는 사람이 서운할 수 있는 모습이에요. 화가 나서 그런 것일 수도, 그냥 성격일 수도 있어요. ㅂ불규칙이라서 '퉁명스러워요', '퉁명스러운'으로 바뀌고, 보통 '말투/대답/목소리'와 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 퉁명스러운 말투 때문에 오해를 받아요.
phrases.en: He gets misunderstood because of his curt way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때 쓰는 활용형이에요. '말투, 대답, 표정'과 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun. It often goes with words like speech style, answer, and expression.

phrases.example: 오늘 친구가 좀 퉁명스러워요. 무슨 일이 있나 봐요.
phrases.en: My friend is a bit curt today. Maybe something happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ불규칙 활용이고, 해요체로 지금 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An irregular ㅂ conjugation in polite speech, used to describe how someone is acting now.

phrases.en: He answered the question curtly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여서 행동을 설명할 때 써요. 말이나 행동이 친절하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-게' lets you describe an action. Used when words or manner are unfriendly.

explain_en: It describes words or behavior that are unfriendly and brusque, which can hurt the listener's feelings. It might be from anger or just personality. It's a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes '퉁명스러워요' and '퉁명스러운', and it usually goes with '말투', '대답' or '목소리'.

examples.en: Grandfather came into the room clearing his throat.
He felt awkward and only cleared his throat.
Before the presentation, I cleared my throat to get ready.
Suddenly I heard someone clearing their throat behind me.
When the children heard their father's throat-clearing, they went quiet.
It was hard to answer, so I got through it with a throat-clear.

explain: 감기 때문에 나오는 '기침'과 달리, '헛기침'은 아프지 않은데 일부러 하는 기침이에요. 어색할 때, 자기가 왔다는 걸 알릴 때, 주의를 끌 때 해요. 보통 '헛기침을 하다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: I heard a throat-clearing sound outside the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 왔다는 신호로 들리는 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The sound that signals someone has arrived.

phrases.en: My father signaled by clearing his throat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말 대신 기침으로 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when signaling with a cough instead of words.
phrases.en_equiv: to signal by clearing one's throat

phrases.example: 헛기침을 두어 번 하고 말을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: He cleared his throat a couple of times and began to speak.
phrases.nuance_ko: '두어 번'은 한두 번 정도라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 두어 번 means about once or twice.

explain_en: Unlike '기침' (a cough from a cold), '헛기침' is done on purpose when you aren't sick. People do it when feeling awkward, to announce their presence, or to get attention. It is usually used as '헛기침을 하다'.

en: to be slim; to be slender; to be thin

examples.en: I've lost weight lately, so my face looks thin.

examples.ko: 동생은 키가 크고 몸이 홀쭉한 편이에요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is tall and on the slim side.
After being sick for a few days, my cheeks became quite hollow.

examples.ko: 이 바지는 다리가 홀쭉해 보이게 만들어 줘요.
examples.en: These pants make your legs look slim.

examples.ko: 홀쭉한 병에 꽃을 한 송이 꽂았어요.
examples.en: I put a single flower in a slim bottle.

examples.ko: 그 모델은 얼굴이 작고 허리도 홀쭉해서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: That model has a small face and a slim waist, so she stands out.

explain: '마르다'는 살이 적은 상태 전체를 말하고, '홀쭉하다'는 얼굴, 볼, 배, 병처럼 길쭉하고 가운데가 들어간 모양에 잘 어울려요. '날씬하다'는 보기 좋다는 칭찬 느낌이 있지만 '홀쭉하다'는 그냥 모양을 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '통통하다'예요.

phrases.en: After being sick, my face became gaunt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴 모양을 설명할 때 '홀쭉한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'holjjukhan' to describe the shape of a face.

phrases.en: After not eating for a few days, my belly became hollow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양이 변해서 가늘어졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the shape became thinner.

phrases.en: I've had a lot of work lately, so my cheeks are sunken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 볼이 들어가 보일 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when cheeks look sunken.

explain_en: '마르다' describes being thin in general, while '홀쭉하다' fits long, narrow shapes with a hollow look, like a face, cheeks, a belly or a bottle. '날씬하다' sounds like a compliment, but '홀쭉하다' just describes the shape. A word with the opposite feel is '통통하다'.
